To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the cancer stem cells in each tumor are a small population of cancer cells that express a specific set of surface markers and 2) the cancer stem cell population in each tumor is heterogeneous and is comprised of cancer cells that differ in the set of surface markers they express, the number of surface markers they display, the level of expression of each marker, and the level of expression and activity of the receptors for the cytokines and hormones that regulate their proliferation and survival.
monoclonal antibodies directed against cell surface located antigens, when coupled to a safe anti-tumor compound, can be used to target the compound to cancer cells, thus enhancing its efficacy.

the use of a combination of therapeutic agents, such as monoclonal antibodies against cell membrane located ectopically expressed molecules and vaccines against the same molecules, can be used to treat cancers that become refractory to drugs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel approaches for treatment of cancers refractory to conventional therapies.
the development of novel immunological approaches to the treatment of cancer.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies that will help in the management of cancers that are refractory to drugs and are metastasized.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
immunotherapy is a safe and effective approach for treating refractory advanced stage cancers.

a combined therapeutic approach using more than one agent, and employing a variety of antibodies and vaccines is the most effective way of dealing with advanced stage cancers that are refractory to drugs.
immunotherapeutic approaches are promising, but need to be further explored and tested in clinical settings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
immunologically targeted therapy is a safe and promising treatment for cancers that have become resistant to available drugs.
immunotherapy of cancers is a promising approach for treatment of refractory tumors.
the heterogeneity of cells in a tumor is a major hurdle in the treatment of cancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
immunological approaches can provide a lasting treatment for advanced cancers refractory to drugs.
the combined approach is likely to be effective in killing the cancer cells and preventing metastases.
the heterogeneity of cancer cell populations can be overcome by a combined approach employing monoclonal antibodies, vaccines and drugs.
